activities.title: Placeholder: which vertex leaves the queue?

config.prompt: A queue holds A, B and C, with A at the front. You dequeue once. Which vertex comes out?

feedback.b: B is in the middle of the queue. A queue only ever gives up the vertex at its front.
feedback.c: C was added last. Taking the newest item first is what a stack does, not a queue.

hints.body: A queue is first in, first out.
Which vertex has been waiting in the queue the longest?
The front of the queue is the vertex that was added first.
A is at the front, so dequeuing returns A. The queue is then B, C.

activities.title: Placeholder: the order neighbours join the queue

config.prompt: BFS starts at A. A's neighbours are C and B. In which order are they added to the queue?

feedback.cb: In this course neighbours are always taken in alphabetical order of their labels, whatever order they are listed in.
feedback.b: BFS adds every neighbour it has not discovered yet, not only the first one.

hints.body: BFS adds all of a vertex's undiscovered neighbours before moving on.
The order neighbours are listed in does not decide the order they are taken in.
Neighbours are taken in alphabetical order of their labels.
B comes before C alphabetically, so B is added first, then C. The queue is B, C.
